title.value: Bronchoscopic Techniques for Surgical Marking and Fiducial Placement

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT-guided transpleural hookwire localization
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Localize small lung nodules for minimally invasive thoracic surgery (MITS) resection.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: After placement of the hook into the target, a wire extended out through the parenchyma then across the pleura to the skin.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Hookwire localization of small lung nodules via CT guidance.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: hemorrhage (9–35%) and pneumothorax (32–68%).

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT-guided microcoil localization
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Percutaneous localization of target nodules to aid intraoperative detection during MITS.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: A needle is inserted to transect the lesion, part of the microcoil is inserted, then remaining length positioned or at pleural line.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Microcoils can be inserted percutaneously to localize target nodules.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Intraoperative localization rates using microcoils have been reported to be excellent (90–100% success) [19].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Methylene blue dye marking
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Dye marking to aid target nodule localization during MITS.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Applied via CT guidance or bronchoscopy to tattoo pleura and/or lesion.
limitations: Narrow utility window and spillage risk.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Used to visually mark lesions for intraoperative localization.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Narrow window of utility (<3 hours) and risk of “spillage” contaminating pleural space

diagnostic_approaches.name: Near-infrared/ICG fluorescent dye marking
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Fluorescent marking to localize deeper nodules during MITS.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Applied via CT guidance or bronchoscopy for NIR visualization.
limitations: may be too deep to see.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When deeper visualization is needed under NIR.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Marking can be seen buried in a 1–2 cm tissue

diagnostic_approaches.name: Barium radiopaque marking
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Radiopaque marking for lesion localization.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Used alone or with dyes to mark lesions.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: As a radiopaque marker to guide localization.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Needs to be tumor “adjacent” due to risk of inflammation impacting pathology result

diagnostic_approaches.name: Lipiodol (ethiodized oil) radiopaque marking
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Radiopaque marker to guide thoracoscopic surgery; long residency.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Injected as a radiopaque marker; can be combined with cyanoacrylates.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Used to guide thoracoscopic surgery; reported use as fiducial prior to radiotherapy.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: seen in situ up to 8 months postplacement [24].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Technetium-99 radiotracer localization
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Radiotracer-guided localization for VATS without fluoroscopy.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Injected via CT-guided percutaneous or bronchoscopic placement; detected by handheld gamma ray detector.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: To achieve high VATS localization without intraoperative fluoroscopy.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: radiotracers have been shown to confer high rates of VATS localization (88–96%) [19].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Electromagnetic Navigation Bronchoscopy (ENB) nodule marking
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Bronchoscopic marking and fiducial placement with real-time navigation.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Uses CT-based 3D airway maps and electromagnetic navigation to reach target for marker placement.
limitations: Lower pneumothorax and hemorrhage than CT-guided marking
can be done same setting as resection.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Marking nodules, including hard-to-reach locations, for surgery.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: reported accurate FM placement in 99.2% of patients with 94.1% of markers durably in place.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Bronchoscopic peripheral navigation with rEBUS/CBCT/digital tomosynthesis for marking
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Localize peripheral nodules and deliver marking medium bronchoscopically.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Use navigation platform, rEBUS and/or cone-beam CT or digital tomosynthesis; puncture with transbronchial needle; inject marking medium; tattoo pleura.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When lesion is not visible and tool-to-target colocalization is needed.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: between 0.5 and 1 ml are needed [30–32].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Self-expanding polyethylene glycol hydrogel marker
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Implantable visual marker designed to improve localization and potentially reduce pneumothorax.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Deploys as a solid cylinder that self-expands upon contact with lung tissue.
limitations: purported sealing of CT access tract to prevent pneumothorax.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: As an engineered implantable marking medium.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: deploys as a solid cylinder (2.5 cm in length by 0.1 cm in diameter), self-expands upon contact with lung tissue

diagnostic_approaches.name: Implantable infrared reflector with audible radar rangefinder
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Implantable marker enabling intraoperative localization without fluoroscopy.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Placed under CT guidance; remains in place; intraoperative audible radar rangefinder guides surgeon.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: To detangle radiology and OR schedules; implant can remain in place.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: pneumothorax and hemothorax were low (9.5% and 0%, respectively) [19]

diagnostic_approaches.name: Intraoperative molecular imaging (Folate receptor NIR markers)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: IV molecular imaging to localize and guide resection of malignant nodules.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Inject NIR dye linked to molecules that accumulate in malignant tissue; visualize intraoperatively.
limitations: influenced intraoperative decisions in 26% of patients (phase 2).
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: To identify nodules and margins intraoperatively via simple infusion.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: paired folate receptor NIR markers have been reported to successfully identify 70–95% of intraoperative nodules [34].

diagnostic_approaches.name: SBRT systems without fiducials (FM-less tracking) criteria
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Track targets for SBRT without fiducial markers when lesions meet visibility criteria.
criteria_or_scoring: Require nodules larger than 15 mm and denser than surrounding parenchyma.
limitations: Limited to lesions meeting size and density criteria.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When tumors are directly trackable without FMs.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: they require nodules to be larger than 15 mm, denser than the surrounding parenchymal tissue

diagnostic_approaches.name: 3D airway navigation mapping (ENB or fiberoptic light shape sensing)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Provide real-time bronchoscopic guidance to peripheral lesions.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Create three-dimensional maps from CT scans; use ENB or light shape sensing to guide to the target lesion.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: To improve intraprocedural navigation for peripheral lesions.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: These systems use electromagnetic navigation (ENB) or fiberoptic light shape sensing with three-dimensional maps to provide real-time guidance through the airways to a target lesion.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Real-time tumor tracking using fiducial markers with orthogonal X-rays and optical monitoring
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Track the moving tumor target and enable respiratory gating in real time during SBRT.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Radiopaque fiducials are implanted near the tumor and light-emitting diodes are placed on the chest. Orthogonal X-ray images during the respiratory cycle build a model relating LED and fiducial positions for tracking.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: The radiation beam tracks the moving tumor target; periodic orthogonal X-rays validate and update the model with breathing pattern changes.
limitations: Lesions must be enough away from the mediastinum for the system to detect.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: An important part of SBRT planning and execution to track and respiratory gate the target tumor in real time.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The total system accuracy of the device and the respiratory motion tracking has been reported as <1 mm.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy (ENB/EMN) for fiducial marker delivery
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Bronchoscopic delivery of fiducial markers to enable tumor tracking for SBRT.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Peripheral navigation bronchoscopy (e.g., ENB, rEBUS, robotic bronchoscopy) guides to the target; fiducials are deployed via a delivery catheter or brush at the level of the target.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Viable and safe alternative for placing fiducial markers with optimal distribution to avoid colinear placement.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: EMN bronchoscopy for FM delivery, reported a 94.1% rate of successful FM placement based on postplacement imaging (most imaging performed same day as procedure) with a 5.4% pneumothorax rate [26].

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT-guided percutaneous fiducial marker placement
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Percutaneous placement of fiducial markers for subsequent tumor tracking.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Percutaneous CT-guided insertion; often requires two punctures with markers placed along tracts.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Colinear placement risk can reduce SBRT tracking accuracy.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Placement via percutaneous methods conveys a risk of pneumothorax similar to or higher than percutaneous lung biopsy (13–48%) [36, 37]

diagnostic_approaches.name: Convex EBUS or fluoroscopic guidance for fiducial deployment
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Imaging-guided implantation of fiducial markers into tumor targets.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: A 22-gauge TBNA needle preloaded with a 0.35 mm coiled wire fiducial is passed through an endobronchial ultrasound scope into the tumor, then deployed under imaging.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: During implantation in central tumors under EBUS/fluoroscopic guidance.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: posterior-anterior fluoroscopic image of a standard 22-gauge TBNA needle preloaded with a 0.35 mm coiled wire ﬁducial being passed through an endobronchial ultrasound scope and into the tumor target

diagnostic_approaches.name: Inter-fiducial distance measurement at the same respiratory phase to detect migration
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Detect and identify fiducial marker migration after implantation.
criteria_or_scoring: Compare distances between fiducials at the same respiratory phase
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Measure the distance between pairs of fiducials at the same phase of respiration; with ≥3, measure between each marker and the others.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: With only two fiducials, migration is detected but cannot identify which moved; with three or more, the migrated marker can be identified.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Post-implant assessment of fiducial stability.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Migration can be detected by measuring the distance between pairs of FM at the same phase of respiration. When only two FMs have been implanted, it is possible to tell

diagnostic_approaches.name: Postplacement imaging to confirm fiducial position and detect migration
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Rule out pneumothorax and confirm appropriate fiducial placement; detect early migration.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Obtain imaging immediately after placement to rule out pneumothorax and CT at 1–2 weeks to confirm placement.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Migration typically occurs within the first 10 days and can be identified on follow-up imaging.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Immediately postprocedure and at 1–2 weeks after fiducial implantation.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: placement should be conﬁrmed 1–2 weeks post- placement with a CT, as migration typically occurs within the ﬁrst 10 days of placement [39, 40].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Fiducial marker spatial criteria for optimal tracking and rotational information
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Ensure fiducials provide independent positional and rotational information for accurate tracking.
criteria_or_scoring: At least three fiducials bracketing the tumor
no more than 5–6 cm from the lesion
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Place fiducials in and around the tumor, ensuring spacing and orientation to avoid superimposition and provide independent information.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Three fiducials that do not overlap on fluoroscopy provide both translational and rotational information.
limitations: they appear superimposed and do not provide useful information
may be outside the tracking system’s field of view.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: During fiducial implantation planning for SBRT tracking.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: In total, FMs should be a minimum of 1.5 cm apart and should be no more than 5–6 cm from the lesion

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT-body anatomic mapping for bronchoscopic navigation to target lesion
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Navigate to peripheral lung lesions for fiducial placement/biopsy.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Use CT-body anatomic mapping to traverse to the target; insert rEBUS probe and guide sheath through the bronchoscope’s working channel upon reaching the target.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Identify the target nodule on radial EBUS before deploying the fiducial.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: During peripheral navigation bronchoscopy for fiducial placement.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: CT-body anatomic mapping was used by bronchoscopists to traverse the lung to the target lesion where upon reaching the target the rEBUS probe and guide sheath were inserted through the working channel

diagnostic_approaches.name: Fiducial-less SBRT tumor tracking systems (FM-free)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Apply SBRT without the need for fiducial markers.
limitations: Limitations exist for nodules less than 15 mm
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Explored as newer systems attempting SBRT without fiducials.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Newer systems have attempted to apply SBRT without the need for FMs; however, limitations exist for nodules less than 15 mm, ground glass nodules, or those near the mediastinum

clinical_guidelines.title: Fiducial quantity for SBRT
clinical_guidelines.condition: Fiducial marker implantation for stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT)
specific_recommendations: Implant 3–6 fiducials so that three remain in place.
decision_points_and_pathways: Plan to place 3–6 fiducials to ensure at least three remain for tracking.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: 3–6 should be implanted to so that three remain in place, they should be placed in and around the tumor

clinical_guidelines.title: Fiducial spacing and arrangement for SBRT
clinical_guidelines.condition: Fiducial marker implantation for stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT)
specific_recommendations: Place fiducials at least 2–5 cm apart.
Arrange fiducials to bracket the bulk of the tumor.
Fiducials placed outside the tumor should be as close to the tumor edge as possible.
Avoid placing fiducials collinearly.
decision_points_and_pathways: Ensure inter-fiducial spacing of at least 2–5 cm.
Confirm configuration brackets the tumor bulk and is non-collinear.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: at a distance of at least 2–5 cm from each other and such that the bulk of the tumor is bracketed by the ﬁducials, those placed outside the tumor should

clinical_guidelines.title: Marker placement considerations for MITS
clinical_guidelines.condition: Target marking for minimally invasive thoracic surgery (MITS)
specific_recommendations: Preoperative discussion with the surgical team is important if markers are implanted by a separate team.
Place markers so they are visible from the visceral pleura.
Include the whole of the target volume to ensure complete resection without margin involvement.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: preoperative discussion with the surgical team is important if the markers are to be implanted by a separate team. In addition, the marker(s) should be placed such that they are visible from the visceral pleura

clinical_guidelines.title: Recommended volume of marking media for bronchoscopic localization
clinical_guidelines.condition: Bronchoscopic delivery of marking medium for surgical localization
specific_recommendations: Deliver between 0.5 and 1 ml of marking medium.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: previously published data would suggest between 0.5 and 1 ml are needed

clinical_guidelines.title: Single-anesthesia approach for ENB marking and resection
clinical_guidelines.condition: Navigation bronchoscopy nodule marking with same-setting surgical resection
specific_recommendations: Consider a single-anesthesia approach where possible to reduce time to intervention.
decision_points_and_pathways: If resources allow, coordinate ENB marking and surgical resection in the same anesthesia session.
outcome_measures: Reduced time to intervention by 51 days on average.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: This “single-anesthesia” approach has been shown to reduce time to intervention by 51 days on average and should be considered where possible

clinical_guidelines.title: USPSTF low-dose CT lung cancer screening
clinical_guidelines.condition: Lung cancer screening in high-risk individuals
specific_recommendations: High-risk individuals aged 50–80 with ≥20 pack-years who currently smoke or quit within 15 years should undergo LDCT screening.
decision_points_and_pathways: If age 50–80 AND ≥20 pack-years AND current smoker or quit <15 years, THEN undergo LDCT LCS.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: High-risk individuals aged 50–80; ≥20 pack-years; current smoker or quit within 15 years.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: USPSTF now recommends that high-risk individuals, aged 50–80 with a 20 or more-pack year smoking history who are currently smoking or quit within the last 15 years, undergo LDCT LCS

clinical_guidelines.title: Preference for SBRT in early-stage lung cancer when resection not pursued
clinical_guidelines.condition: Treatment selection for early-stage lung cancer when patient unable or unwilling to undergo resection
specific_recommendations: SBRT is preferred for tumors less than 5 cm where normal tissue dose constraints can be respected.
decision_points_and_pathways: If tumor <5 cm and normal tissue dose constraints can be respected, prefer SBRT.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: with stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) preferred for tumors less than 5 cm where normal tissue dose constraints can be respected

clinical_guidelines.title: Management of nodules with moderate- to high-risk of malignancy
clinical_guidelines.condition: Pulmonary nodules with moderate- to high-risk pretest probability for malignancy
specific_recommendations: Consider surgical resection or biopsy with patient-provider shared decision-making.
decision_points_and_pathways: If pretest probability is moderate to high, consider resection or biopsy with shared decision-making.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Pulmonary nodules with moderate- to high-risk pretest probability for malignancy.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: those nodules with a moderate- to high-risk pretest probability for malignancy should be considered for surgical resection or biopsy in conjunction with patient-provider shared decision-making.

clinical_guidelines.title: Radiotracer (technetium-99) timing and handling for surgical localization
clinical_guidelines.condition: Use of radiotracers to localize target nodules for thoracoscopic surgery
specific_recommendations: No intraoperative fluoroscopy is required.
Radiation protection and proper radioactive material handling are required.
With a half-life of about 6 hours, surgery must occur soon after marking.
decision_points_and_pathways: If using technicium99, schedule surgery soon after marking due to ~6-hour half-life.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: With a half-life of about 6 hours, surgery must occur soon after marking but with more ﬂexibility than traditional nonﬂuorescent dyes.

clinical_guidelines.title: Recommended number of fiducial markers to implant
clinical_guidelines.condition: Fiducial marker implantation
specific_recommendations: 3–6 FMs should be implanted to so that at least three remain in place.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: 3–6 FMs should be implanted to so that at least three remain in place.

clinical_guidelines.title: Inter-marker spacing between fiducials
clinical_guidelines.condition: Fiducial marker implantation
specific_recommendations: FMs should be placed such that they are at least 1.5 cm but not more than 5 cm from each other.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: FMs should be placed such that they are at least 1.5 cm but not more than 5 cm from each other.

clinical_guidelines.title: Avoid collinear fiducial placement
clinical_guidelines.condition: Fiducial marker implantation
specific_recommendations: FMs should not be placed collinearly.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: FMs should not be placed collinearly.

clinical_guidelines.title: Bracket tumor with fiducials
clinical_guidelines.condition: Fiducial marker implantation around tumor target
specific_recommendations: FMs should be placed in and around the tumor such that the bulk of the tumor is bracketed by the fiducials.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: FMs should be placed in and around the tumor such that the bulk of the tumor is bracketed by the ﬁducials.

clinical_guidelines.title: Fiducial spacing from lesion and orientation
clinical_guidelines.condition: Fiducial marker positioning relative to lesion for targeting
specific_recommendations: FMs should be a minimum of 1.5 cm apart.
FMs should be no more than 5–6 cm from the lesion.
FMs should be oriented differently in the x, y, and z planes.
Avoid positioning such that a straight line can be drawn between any three fiducials; avoid superimposition on fluoroscopy.
Ensure markers are within the field of view of the tracking system.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: In total, FMs should be a minimum of 1.5 cm apart and should be no more than 5–6 cm from the lesion

clinical_guidelines.title: Information provided by two fiducial markers
clinical_guidelines.condition: Fiducial marker number and tracking capability
specific_recommendations: Two FMs bracketing the tumor can provide translational information about the tumor target.
decision_points_and_pathways: With only two FMs, you can detect movement but not identify which marker migrated.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Two FM located in and around the tumor such that they bracket the bulk of the tumor can provide translational information about the tumor target.

clinical_guidelines.title: Information provided by three fiducial markers
clinical_guidelines.condition: Fiducial marker number and tracking capability
specific_recommendations: Three FMs that bracket the tumor and do not overlap on fluoroscopy provide both translational and rotational information.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Three FMs located in and around the tumor such that they bracket the bulk of the tumor and do not overlap on the ﬂuoroscopic tracking system provide both translational and rotational

clinical_guidelines.title: Identifying migrated fiducials with three or more markers
clinical_guidelines.condition: Fiducial marker migration detection strategy
specific_recommendations: With three or more FMs, measure inter-marker distances to identify which marker migrated; ignore the migrated FM for tracking.
decision_points_and_pathways: If three or more FMs implanted → identify which fiducial migrated by pairwise distance checks.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: When three or more FMs have been implanted, by measuring the distance between each marker and the others, it is possible to tell not only that one has migrated but

clinical_guidelines.title: Postplacement imaging schedule
clinical_guidelines.condition: Monitoring after fiducial marker implantation
specific_recommendations: Obtain imaging immediately after placement to rule out pneumothorax.
Obtain imaging 1–2 weeks after placement to confirm appropriate placement.
monitoring_requirements: Immediate postplacement imaging to rule out pneumothorax.
Imaging at 1–2 weeks to confirm placement.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Postplacement imaging should be obtained immediately after placement to rule out pneumothorax and 1–2 weeks after placement of FMs to conﬁrm appropriate placement.

clinical_guidelines.title: Confirm placement due to early migration risk
clinical_guidelines.condition: Monitoring and timing after fiducial placement
specific_recommendations: Confirm placement 1–2 weeks post-placement with CT because migration typically occurs within the first 10 days.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: placement should be conﬁrmed 1–2 weeks post- placement with a CT, as migration typically occurs within the ﬁrst 10 days of placement

clinical_guidelines.title: Fiducial migration risk percentage
clinical_guidelines.condition: Fiducial marker migration risk after placement
specific_recommendations: Be aware that fiducials are at risk for migration (up to 12%).
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: FMs themselves are at risk for migration (up to 12%),

clinical_guidelines.title: Bronchoscopic placement as a safe alternative
clinical_guidelines.condition: Approach to fiducial marker placement (bronchoscopic vs percutaneous)
specific_recommendations: Placement via bronchoscopy helps mitigate risk and is a viable and safe alternative for placing FMs.
This approach allows optimal distribution of FMs to avoid colinear placement.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Placement via bronchoscopy helps mitigate risk to the patient and is a viable and safe alternative for placing FMs.

clinical_guidelines.title: Percutaneous fiducial placement pneumothorax risk
clinical_guidelines.condition: Risk counseling for percutaneous fiducial placement
specific_recommendations: Recognize pneumothorax risk with percutaneous methods (13–48%).
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Placement via percutaneous methods conveys a risk of pneumothorax similar to or higher than percutaneous lung biopsy (13–48%)

clinical_guidelines.title: Guidance modality for fiducial deployment
clinical_guidelines.condition: Intra-procedural guidance for fiducial deployment
specific_recommendations: Perform deployment under either convex EBUS or fluoroscopic guidance.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Deployment is performed under either convex EBUS or ﬂuoroscopic guidance (Fig. 5)

clinical_guidelines.title: Needle withdrawal technique after FM implantation
clinical_guidelines.condition: Technique to prevent fiducial displacement during withdrawal
specific_recommendations: Withdraw the needle slowly after implantation to ensure the fiducial has cleared the outer barrel of the needle.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Once implanted, the needle should be withdrawn slowly to ensure that the ﬁducial has cleared the outer barrel of needle.

clinical_guidelines.title: Needle tip positioning before deployment
clinical_guidelines.condition: Positioning for fiducial implantation via bronchoscopy
specific_recommendations: Advance the catheter tip to approximately 1–2 cm proximal to the desired implantation site before extending the needle.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: and is approximately 1–2 cm proximal to the desired implantation site.

clinical_guidelines.title: Respiratory gating alignment
clinical_guidelines.condition: Patient alignment for respiratory-gated radiation
specific_recommendations: Align the patient so that the beam is on during expiration.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The patient is typically aligned so that the beam is on during expiration.

clinical_guidelines.title: Use perioperative imaging to confirm FM spatial relationships
clinical_guidelines.condition: Intra-procedural confirmation during fiducial placement
specific_recommendations: Use advanced perioperative imaging to help confirm spatial relationships between FMs during placement.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Advanced perioperative imaging (integrated or not) can be used to help conﬁrm the spatial relationships between the FMs as they are being placed.

clinical_guidelines.title: Spacing for subsequent fiducial placements
clinical_guidelines.condition: Sequential fiducial placement strategy
specific_recommendations: Place subsequent FMs at least 1.5 cm but not more than 5 cm from each other.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: they be at least 1.5 cm but not more than 5 cm from each other.

clinical_guidelines.title: Limitations of SBRT without fiducials
clinical_guidelines.condition: Use of SBRT without fiducial markers
specific_recommendations: Note limitations for nodules less than 15 mm, ground glass nodules, or those near the mediastinum or spine.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Nodules less than 15 mm, ground glass nodules, or near mediastinum or spine
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: limitations exist for nodules less than 15 mm, ground glass nodules, or those near the mediastinum or spine.

clinical_guidelines.title: Choice of coil-shaped fiducials to reduce migration
clinical_guidelines.condition: Selection of fiducial marker type
specific_recommendations: Consider coil-shaped fiducials as they are thought to retain positioning better than seed- or dumbbell-shaped FMs.
contraindications_and_exceptions: Must fit through the working channel of the bronchoscope/catheter.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Coil-shaped ﬁducials are thought to retain their positioning better than seed- or dumbbell-shaped FMs

clinical_guidelines.title: Example deployment tools (central tumor under EBUS)
clinical_guidelines.condition: Instrumentation for EBUS-guided fiducial implantation
specific_recommendations: Use a standard 22-gauge TBNA needle preloaded with a 0.35 mm coiled wire fiducial.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: a standard 22-gauge TBNA needle pre- loaded with a 0.35 mm coiled wire ﬁducial

figures.caption: Generic margin expansion to accommodate microscopic tumor extension beyond the radiographic borders of the tumor, errors that occur in daily patient positioning, and tumor movement secondary to respiratory motion. (a) Shows a generic tumor. The lightly dashed line represents the margin expansion added to increase the volume of planned radiation delivery to accommodate microscopic tumor extension beyond the radiographic borders of the tumor. (b) Shows the same generic tumor with its expanded margin as it might appear on three separate days. The variability in position is related to errors in daily patient positioning. figures.caption: Fig. 2 A small 6-MV linac mounted on a computer-controlled robotic arm capable of moving with 6° of freedom, two orthogonally placed X-rays, two optical cameras, and an optic-radiographic motion monitoring system for real-time tumor tracking. Radio-opaque ﬁducial markers implanted in or near the tumor and light-emitting diodes placed on the patient’s chest are used for target tracking. Prior to radiation treatment and while the X-ray beam is off, a series of X-ray images are taken by the two orthogonal cameras at various times during the respiratory cycle, and the system develops a mathematical model relating the locations of the light-emitting diodes on the chest with those of the ﬁducials near the tumor in the lung. Continuous tracking of the light-emitting diodes combined with this mathematical model allows the robotic arm to be moved in real time such that the radiation beam tracks the moving tumor target. At regular intervals during treatment, additional orthogonal X-ray images are taken to allow the model to be validated and updated with small changes in breathing patterns. The current system allows for a dozen different beam directions from over a hundred different robot arm locations, providing more than 1200 possible beam paths. (a) Shows an overview of the SBRTsystem with a patient positioned on the couch. (b) Demonstrates the motion capabilities of the linac system. (Images used by permission of Accuray Incorporated)

definitions.content: One technique uses multiple radiation beams directed at the tumor from multiple different angles, thereby “focusing” the radiation beams on a small volume of tissue. The shape of each beam is also adjusted so that it “conforms” to the contour of the target. This allows the majority of the radiation dose to be delivered to a very focused volume of tissue that has a shape and size very similar to that of the tumor. This is commonly referred to as three-dimensional conformal radiation therapy (3D-CRT).

definitions.content: Real-time tumor tracking is a method of dynamically moving the focal point of the radiation mean so that this focal point always corresponds with the position of the tumor target.

practice_recommendations.content: Some basic guidelines to follow when implanting FM for SBRT include the following: 3–6 should be implanted to so that three remain in place, they should be placed in and around the tumor at a distance of at least 2–5 cm from each other and such that the bulk of the tumor is bracketed by the ﬁducials, those placed outside the tumor should be placed as close to the edge of the tumor as possible, and they should not be placed collinearly.

technology_and_technique.topic: Fiducial placement for SBRT: procedural best practices
technology_and_technique.summary: Implant 3–6 fiducial markers so that ≥3 remain in place; place in and around the tumor, spacing each by 2–5 cm; bracket the bulk of the tumor; markers outside the tumor should be as close to the tumor edge as possible; avoid collinear placement. Fiducials enable accurate localization/tracking even when the tumor is difficult to visualize on fluoroscopy or CT.
technology_and_technique.reference: Michaels A, Mayse ML, Akulian J. Bronchoscopic Techniques for Surgical Marking and Fiducial Placement. Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_59-1 (Chapter abstract)

technology_and_technique.topic: Fiducial placement for MITS (surgical marking) tips
technology_and_technique.summary: Coordinate preoperatively with the surgical team when implantation is performed by a separate team; place marker(s) so they are visible from the visceral pleura and encompass the entire target volume to facilitate complete resection and avoid margin involvement.
technology_and_technique.reference: Michaels A, Mayse ML, Akulian J. 2025 chapter abstract (doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_59-1)

technology_and_technique.topic: Localization challenges and conversion in MITS vs open surgery
technology_and_technique.summary: Digital palpation-based localization is harder for nodules >5 mm from the pleura, <10 mm in size, and/or subsolid. Transition to MITS—especially RATS—reduces haptic feedback, increasing localization difficulty. Reported conversion to open thoracotomy due to localization issues is as high as 50%.

technology_and_technique.topic: Patient selection for surgery vs SBRT
technology_and_technique.summary: USPSTF screening eligibility: age 50–80, ≥20 pack-years, current smoker or quit within 15 years. Nodules with moderate-to-high pretest malignancy probability should undergo surgical resection or biopsy with shared decision-making. ~25% of patients are not candidates for lobectomy due to comorbidities; sublobar resection is recommended and has been shown noninferior or superior to lobar resection in early-stage disease. SBRT is preferred for tumors <5 cm where normal tissue constraints can be respected and is used for inoperable or unwilling surgical candidates.

technology_and_technique.topic: Comparative effectiveness: MITS vs open thoracotomy
technology_and_technique.summary: MITS (VATS/RATS) reduces morbidity compared with open thoracotomy, expanding resection to patients previously considered too ill for surgery. However, localization is more challenging in MITS, contributing to conversion rates to open procedures up to 50% when localization fails.

technology_and_technique.topic: Fiducials vs imaging alone for target tracking
technology_and_technique.summary: Fiducial markers act as reliable surrogates of tumor location, improving localization and motion tracking for SBRT and aiding intraoperative localization for MITS when lesions are not well seen on fluoroscopy or CT.
technology_and_technique.reference: Michaels A, Mayse ML, Akulian J. 2025 chapter abstract (doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_59-1)
